rich_summary: Pandu tells Kunti that the lord of the gods has been pleased by her vow and will grant her a son of unmatched valor. Following his request, Kunti invokes Sakra (Indra), who fathers the child later known as Arjuna. At Arjuna’s birth, a divine voice proclaims his future greatness: he will rival legendary heroes, defeat powerful enemies, aid the Kurus, burn the Khandava forest to satisfy Agni, obtain celestial weapons including Shiva’s Pasupata, and even destroy the fearsome Nivatakavacha demons. The event is celebrated by an immense gathering of gods, sages, Gandharvas, Apsaras, Nagas, and other celestial beings who rejoice and shower blessings upon the newborn. Afterwards Pandu desires more children, but Kunti refuses, citing scriptural limits and social norms regarding multiple partners.

highlight_spans.why: Pandu foretells the extraordinary qualities of the son Kunti will receive from the king of the gods.
The pivotal moment when Kunti invokes Indra and Arjuna is conceived.
The divine proclamation predicting Arjuna’s future feats and legendary status.
The cosmic celebration of Arjuna’s birth with gods, sages, and celestial musicians.
Kunti’s firm refusal to bear another child, invoking scriptural and moral boundaries.

top_scenes.scene_text: Kunti invoking Indra in a quiet mountain hermitage as the radiant king of the gods descends in divine light to grant her a heroic son.
The newborn Arjuna as a celestial voice echoes through the sky while flowers rain down and gods, sages, and Gandharvas gather in the heavens above the mountain.
A vast heavenly festival with Apsaras dancing, Gandharvas singing, and gods assembled in shining chariots celebrating the birth of Pandu’s son.
